mentions.author: djk447
mentions.story: Function pipelines: Building functional programming into PostgreSQL
mentions.text:
(NB: Post author here)

We don't have many Haskell programmers, we mostly work in Rust, C and Go, but we're always open to new things...

This is pretty Postgres specific. From the beginning Postgres has focused on extensibility and allowed this sort of stuff with custom functions/operators/types. Many other SQL variants don't have that. It's one of the main things that sets Postgres apart from other databases, see Stonebreaker's great history of this, specifically the stuff on Object Relational databases [1].

We're pretty focused on building on top of Postgres because of that functionality. We do have some other stuff to make Postgres more scalable, and you're welcome to try us out, but…

mentions.story: Ask HN: What does database (internals) development look like?
mentions.text:
Start by watching Michael Stonebraker's Turing Award lecture, he will give you the lowdown and inspiration:
[link]

Start with relational, understand why it is the reference architecture, and from there the tradeoffs involved and what other architectures bring to the table (columnar, streaming, object, in-memory, array, distributed, blockchain, nosql, etc)

To really understand why you should start with relational, read Stonebraker's classic paper: "What goes around comes around": [course]

It will teach you database evolution history so that you don't end up reinventing the wheel.
